description.narrative:
Somalia Joint Response SomJR is a Dutch Relief Alliance DRA funded consortium of four Dutch organization (Oxfam Novib, Midair, SOS,and WVI) working with eight local partners to deliver humanitarian assistance to the affected population. Out of the eight local partners, four of them are Nexus members, SADO, SSWC, working in South-Central and KAALO working in Puntland where three of them working with Oxfam and TAKOLU working with WVI in Somaliland. The grant started in January 2022 and will continue till end of December 2023 where the consortium deliver assistance in the following sectors: Food Security and livelihoods, WaSH, Protection, Cash, Nutrition, Health, localization, and Accountability. With total budget of over nine million Euros.
Purpose: - Support Nexus platform and promote the role of local humanitarian leadership of newly established entities - Enhance the quality and timeliness of the implementation of SomJR activities and ensure mainstreaming and applying the concept of triple Nexusthrough the SomJR activities
Deliverables: - Lead on meetings with SomJR Nexus members frequently and update Nexus members and steering committee about the progress and contribution of SomJR to improve Nexus performance - Lead on developing and presenting innovative initiatives of implementing Triple Nexus concepts through the delivery of the SomJR activities - Lead on organizing joint exchange/monitoring of activities implemented bythe SOMJR NEXUS members Scope: Timeframe: all the work and initiatives should be developed, implemented, and monitored during the project period which is between 01 January 2022 – 31 December 2023 Organizations: Nexus will be leading and working closely with Nexus members ONLY participating in SomJR (TASCO, SADO, SSWC, KAALO) not all local partners within the consortium. At the same time, itshighly recommended to coordinate with other Nexus members which are not participating in SomJR (CPD, GREDO, WASDA, HAVOYOCO). Funding: Nexus will be responsible of the coordination, monitoring and leading only, while the funding for the initiatives and implementation will be covered by members budget or JR budget. Geographically: Nexus initiatives will be linked to members activities’ locations agreed under the consortium. However, SomJR is a flexible project and if there is a valid justification, locations can be changed

participating-org.narrative: In 2004 Oxfam Novib set up a Liaison Office in Nairobi, Kenya in order to support the Strengthening Somali Civil Society Program, at the request of the EU. This request was based on Oxfam Novib's work in Somalia to date, but intended to be more widely directed atthe entire civil society sector and the specific context in which it is operating in a post-conflict country. The program started with consulting local organisations in Somalia and Somaliland to get a complete picture of the sectors and regions where they are active, the challenges they face and the relationship between civil society, local political structures and the private sector. A program was then developed to strengthen the institutional development of Oxfam Novib's partners and those of other Oxfams, as well as a range of new NGOs. In the first year local consultants were trained in Somalia. They were then seconded to civil society organisations to build their capacity in financial and organisational management. Furthermore, workshops were organised on specific themes suchas human rights and the role of civil society in the Somali context. The Liaison Office is now going to support the expansion of the program, focussing on strengthening both organisation and project management, while facilitating more training in the fields of civic education, governance, human rights and women's rights, HIV and AIDS and child protection. Over the years, the Somalia Country Office has expanded its intervention on short term humanitarian response as well as development development interventions. In 2015/2016, a decision was reached to move the Country Programme operation, which was largely in Nairobi, from Nairobi to Hargeisa. The country office has a small office in Nairobi , Kenya and large operations office in Hargeisa, Somaliland.
